# Contributing to ChannelSurfer

Thanks for your interest in improving ChannelSurfer. This document explains how to
report problems, request features, and submit changes.

## Reporting Bugs

If something isn't working, please open an issue:

https://github.com/channelsurfer-1/ChannelSurfer/issues

Before opening a new issue, search existing ones to avoid duplicates.

When reporting a bug, please include:

- **Operating system and version** (e.g. macOS 15.1, Windows 11, Ubuntu 24.04)
- **ChannelSurfer version** (shown in the app's title bar or about dialog)
- **Steps to reproduce** — what you did, in order
- **What you expected to happen**
- **What actually happened**
- **Screenshots or terminal output**, if relevant

Vague reports like "it doesn't work" are hard to act on. The more detail you
provide, the easier it is to investigate.

## Requesting Features

Feature requests are welcome. Open an issue and describe:

- The problem you're trying to solve
- Your proposed solution, if you have one
- Any alternatives you considered

Not every request will be implemented, but all will be read.

## Pull Requests

Pull requests are welcome for bug fixes, small improvements, and documentation
corrections. For larger changes, please open an issue first to discuss the
approach before writing code.

When submitting a pull request:

- Keep changes focused. One fix or feature per PR.
- Test on at least one platform before submitting. If the change touches
  platform-specific code, test on the relevant platforms.
- Describe what the change does and why in the PR description.
- Reference any related issue (e.g. "Fixes #12").

## Response Expectations

ChannelSurfer is maintained by a single developer on a best-effort basis.
Issues and pull requests will be reviewed as time allows, but no response time
is guaranteed. Please be patient.

## Code of Conduct

Be respectful. This is a small project and there's no room for hostility.
Constructive criticism of the code is fine; personal attacks are not.
